messages:
Elena Rossi: Follow-up from today's design critique: two accessibility & discoverability issues in the routing editor(1) focus states are too subtle when tabbing through rules, (2) preview controls disappear off-screen when the keyboard is open on mobile. Need practical fixes we can ship quickly.

Tom Erickson: For focus states, let's use a 3px high-contrast focus ring that meets 4.5:1 against the surrounding surface. Also add a visible focus indicator for the mini-toolbar buttons and drag handle (keyboard users should see an obvious affordance).

Maya Chen: Agree. Small design constraint: we can't increase vertical spacing in compact mode, so the focus ring needs to sit inside the existing padding. Use an inset focus ring with outline-offset: -2px. Also consider a subtle background tint on focus to help mouse users.

Samir Gupta: Copy/UX note: when a rule row receives keyboard focus, show a concise context label in the left gutter for screen readers: "Focused: Rule \"Set country header\" position 4 of 12".

a11y-bot: Accessibility scan: current focus contrast fails in 7% of simulated themes. Recommendation: provide a themable variable --focus-contrast that defaults to navy (#0b3d91) for light themes and is inverted for dark. Also ensure focusable elements have a min 44px hit target.

Elena Rossi: Mobile preview controls: problem is keyboard (OSK) pushes content up and hides the preview toggle. Proposal: introduce a sticky bottom simulation bar that mirrors the preview toggle + primary controls when the viewport height is constrained. This should appear only when the preview pane is scrolled out of view or when the OSK is visible.

Tom Erickson: Implementation detail: sticky bar should be 56px tall, include aria-label="Simulation actions" and be non-modal. It must not capture focus automatically; instead include a visible button to jump to the full preview. Also provide an escape to close the bar.

Maya Chen: UX microcopy: sticky bar primary button label -> "Open simulation" and secondary toggles keep state in the tooltip: "Preview simulation, off" / "Preview simulation, on". If unsaved changes exist, show a small persistence dot.

Samir Gupta: Validation flow: when validation messages appear, avoid absolute overlays that cover the sticky bar. Convert rule-level validation to an inline helper row that collapses; for global simulation errors show a small dismissible banner above the sticky bar with role="alert". Example copy: "Simulation incomplete  Missing required context: user.region. [View details]".

design-bot: Layout audit: simulated mobile scenarios show 10% overlap of preview toggle when sticky bar not present; introducing sticky bar reduces overlap to 1.2%. Also flagged: sticky bar must respect CSS env(safe-area-inset-bottom) for phones with home indicators.

Tom Erickson: Keyboard interactions: when a rule is focused, pressing Space toggles selection; pressing M opens a small move menu (move up/down/top/bottom). After a move, use an aria-live polite region to announce: "Rule 'X' moved to position Y of Z". Also include a 'reorder' mode that traps arrow keys for granular moves but is opt-in.

Maya Chen: For visual polish: add a tiny animation on the sticky bar appearing (scaleY from 0.98 -> 1 over 120ms) and respect prefers-reduced-motion. For the focus ring, use CSS variable --focus-ring-color so product theming can override.

Samir Gupta: I'll draft the exact screen-reader text. Proposal for focus announcement: on focus: "Focused rule: \"{title}\". Press M for move menu. Press Enter to open." For move confirmation: "Moved {title} to {position} of {total}."

a11y-bot: Checklist before handoff: 1) focus contrast >= 4.5:1, 2) all interactive controls >= 44px, 3) aria-live messages present and not duplicative, 4) sticky bar reachable by keyboard and dismissed by ESC.

Elena Rossi: Action items: Tom - prototype focus ring + move menu interactions in storybook; Maya - add sticky simulation bar comp and microcopy; Samir - finalize aria messaging; a11y-bot & design-bot - re-run automated checks. Target: prototype review in 5 working days. Thanks everyone! :sparkles:
